title: What the Great Pyramid looked like in Cleopatra's day
description:
What did the Great Pyramid look like in Cleopatra's day? Not like today: it still wore its smooth, polished outer casing. Cleopatra, born in 69 BC, lived closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramid's building. The Greek historian Diodorus, who visited Egypt when she was a girl, wrote that its stones were still in place, and was told that 360,000 men had spent twenty years building it. Then, in 2013, at Wadi al-Jarf, an ancient harbour on the Red Sea, archaeologists found papyrus documents from the reign of Khufu, the pyramid's own king: the oldest papyri with writing found in Egypt as of 2014. Among them was the logbook of an inspector named Merer, whose boat crew hauled limestone from the Tura quarries, about 17 km away, to the pyramid. They had lain buried for about four and a half thousand years.

Sources:

- Tallet & Marouard 2014, "The Harbor of Khufu on the Red Sea Coast at Wadi al-Jarf, Egypt", Near Eastern Archaeology 77(1), 4-14. doi:10.5615/neareastarch.77.1.0004
- Tallet & Marouard 2016, "The Harbor Facilities of King Khufu on the Red Sea Shore", Journal of the American Research Center in Egypt 52.
- Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37), e2202530119. doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119
